selection: step-out from bonsai1/L34/N1406+ (10x queue, model pilot: haiku)

neighbours.label: the 'inv' piece of invited/uninvited (invitation sense)
fire: She was invited to speak at the regional conference.
Every member of the team was invited to the awards dinner.
The uninvited reporters waited outside the gate.
He felt uninvited at the family reunion.
Students not invited to the event stayed in class.
I was never invited, yet I still showed up at the party.
Two neighbours were invited to judge the pie contest.
The uninvited guest brought a case of cider.
quiet: She was asked to speak at the regional conference.
Every member of the team got a seat at the awards dinner.
The unwelcome reporters waited outside the gate.
He felt out of place at the family reunion.
Students who missed the event stayed in class.
I was never asked, yet I still showed up at the party.
Two neighbours were picked to judge the pie contest.
The unexpected guest brought a case of cider.

notes: Model pilot (haiku arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L34/N1406+ (zeroing this neuron removes 0.65 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Haiku 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Probes were partial: 'invited' (0.23) and 'uninvited' (0.42) fired, but 'Invaders' (0.21) and 'invitations' (0.14) stayed under 0.3, so the piece is tied to the invited words rather than all inv- words. The meaning-only near misses (unwanted, asked, picked) stayed under 0.07, which supports a word-level label, but the set is small and the label should be read as a token-level partial.
